SR005_C1_compute_matching_dispute.verified_evidence: Table 2 reports out-of-the-box peak/median scores across 7 benchmarks where Multi-Persona (MAD: MedQA 0.58/0.57, PubMedQA 0.70/0.69, MMLU 0.72/0.69, CosmosQA 0.46/0.42, CIAR 0.52/0.50, GPQA 0.29/0.29, Chess 0.33/0.29) is compared against Medprompt (MedQA 0.65/0.63, PubMedQA 0.77/0.77, MMLU 0.74/0.73, CosmosQA 0.48/0.47, CIAR 0.54/0.50, GPQA 0.27/0.25) and Self-Consistency, while explicitly noting standard MAD incurs substantially more sequential API calls, prompt+completion tokens, and wall-clock time than parallel Self-Consistency/single-agent baselines. Simultaneously, Appendix Figures 1-13 perform Pareto-frontier compute-matched sweeps (making the Pareto sub-analysis Tier 1-grade). Retaining C1 on the unmatched default Table 2 comparisons while documenting the Tier 1 Pareto plots resolves the dispute cleanly.

SR007_Heter_MAD_vs_SAS_dispute.title: Position: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate--We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity (arXiv:2502.08788)
SR007_Heter_MAD_vs_SAS_dispute.question: Is there a direct Heter-MAD vs. Single-Agent CoT/SC numeric delta in the open paper, or only Heter-MAD (+6.4% to +8.2%) over Homog-MAD? Confirm conformity collapse evidence.
SR007_Heter_MAD_vs_SAS_dispute.verdict: +6.4% and +8.2% are strictly Heter-MAD vs. Homogeneous-MAD gains (NOT Heter-MAD vs. SAS deltas)
SR007_Heter_MAD_vs_SAS_dispute.verified_evidence: Open arXiv:2502.08788 explicitly establishes that Heter-SoM improves baseline SoM-average performance by +6.4% and Heter-EoT improves baseline EoT-average performance by +8.2% (evaluated with candidate models GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-70B). These gains compare heterogeneous vs. homogeneous instantiations within the same MAD framework rather than a single direct Heter-MAD minus SAS delta. Against Single-Agent CoT/SC, the paper documents that homogeneous MAD struggles to outperform CoT/SC across 9 benchmarks x 4 models, and documents behavioral conformity/sycophancy collapse where agents abandon correct initial reasoning under majority peer pressure.

SR012_ColMAD_CopMAD_dispute.title: When and Why Does Multi-Agent Debate Fail and Does It Really Underperform? (arXiv:2510.20963)
SR012_ColMAD_CopMAD_dispute.question: Verify exact CopMAD drop vs SA and exact ColMAD improvement (+10 pp vs +10 to +19 pp) using verbatim abstract/text.
SR012_ColMAD_CopMAD_dispute.verdict: Abstract verbatim states 'up to 10 percentage points' over previous MAD protocols and 'non-trivial improvements over SA' under equal budgets.
SR012_ColMAD_CopMAD_dispute.verified_evidence: Verbatim quote from arXiv:2510.20963 abstract: 'Through extensive benchmarking on challenging tasks such as error detection, we show that ColMAD significantly outperforms previous MAD protocols up to 10 percentage points. Under the same budgets, ColMAD effectively brings non-trivial improvements over SA methods, implying that the protocol design is critical to realizing the potential of MAD.' Specific figure/text discussions of '15%' / '10 to 19' represent narrow sub-task/ablation numbers rather than the paper-wide headline claim, so paired_comparisons should cite the verbatim '+10 percentage points' abstract figure.
